title: Rotational kinematics; Torque; Moment of inertia; · part 1 of 1; Moments and static equilibrium; Newton's second law for rotation
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Mechanics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: R01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; R01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; R01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; R02-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D08-1#N.5b, R01-1#N.2, R02-1#N.2, R03-1#N.2, R03-calc-1#N.3, R04-1#N.1, D08-1#N.9, R01-1#N.5b, R02-1#N.5b, R03-1#N.4b, R03-calc-1#N.7, R04-1#N.5b.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Rigid system
items.clue: Body that keeps its shape, so every point shares the same ω and α.

items.label: Tangential acceleration
items.clue: Linear quantity equal to rα for a point at distance r from the axis.

items.label: Radian
items.clue: Unit of θ, defined by arc length over r; one revolution is 2π of them.

items.label: Lever arm
items.clue: Perpendicular distance from the axis to the line of action of the force.

questions.stem: A uniform board of mass 3.0 kg and length 2.0 m rests horizontally on a pivot 0.60 m from its left end. What mass must be placed at the left end of the board for it to remain balanced?
A disc on a fixed axle rotates 1.0 revolution counter-clockwise and then 0.25 revolution clockwise. Counter-clockwise is taken as positive. What is the disc's angular displacement?
A wheel turns on a fixed axle through its centre. Four forces, each of 20 N and each in the plane of the wheel, act on it one at a time. Which force exerts no torque about the axle?

options.text: A force at the rim, at 45° to the spoke that joins that point to the centre.
A force halfway along a spoke, perpendicular to that spoke.
A force at the rim, pulling outward along the line of the spoke.
A force at the rim, along the tangent to the rim at that point.

questions.explanation: Its line of action passes through the axle (θ = 0°), so sin θ = 0 and the torque is zero, however large the force.

questions.stem: A bicycle wheel can rotate about its axle. Which change would increase the wheel's rotational inertia about the axle?

options.text: Moving some of its mass from the rim in towards the hub
Spinning the wheel at a faster rate about the same axle
Pushing on the rim, rather than near the hub, to turn it
Moving some of its mass from the hub out to the rim

questions.stem: A thin uniform rod of mass 2.0 kg and length 1.2 m rotates about an axis perpendicular to the rod through a point 0.30 m from one end. Using I = ∫ r² dm, what is the rod's rotational inertia about this axis?
A rigid wheel turns on a fixed axle. The net torque exerted on the wheel is not zero. Which statement about the wheel must be true?

options.text: Its angular velocity is changing with time.
It turns in the same sense as the resultant torque.
Its angular speed is increasing with time.
It turns at a steady rate set by the torque.

questions.stem: An electric fan is switched on, and after a few seconds its blades turn at a constant angular velocity. Which statement about the torques exerted on the blades while they turn at this constant angular velocity is correct?

options.text: The motor's torque is balanced by the opposing torques.
The motor's torque exceeds the torques that oppose the rotation.
The net torque is not zero, since each point on a blade accelerates.
No torques are exerted, since the blades are in equilibrium.

questions.stem: Two identical fans, X and Y, start from rest. Each speeds up with constant angular acceleration until it reaches the same final angular velocity. The angular acceleration of fan X is twice that of fan Y. What is the ratio Δθ_X/Δθ_Y of the angles through which the fans turn while speeding up?

A rod of length 0.60 m can rotate about an axle through one end. A string is attached to the rod 0.40 m from the axle and pulls on it with a force of 50 N directed at 37° to the rod. What is the magnitude of the torque exerted on the rod by the string's force about the axle? Use sin 37° = 0.60 and cos 37° = 0.80.

A small object of mass m is fastened to a light rod a distance r from the rod's axis of rotation. It is replaced by a small object of mass m/3 fastened a distance 3r from the same axis. The new rotational inertia of the system about the axis is how many times the original rotational inertia?

A thin rod of length L and total mass M has linear mass density λ = λ₀x/L, where x is the distance from end A and λ₀ is a positive constant. What is the rod's rotational inertia about an axis through end A, perpendicular to the rod?

A solid disc of radius 0.50 m and rotational inertia 0.25 kg m² turns on a fixed axle. A string wrapped around its rim is pulled with a constant force of 2.0 N, tangent to the rim, in the sense in which the disc is turning. Friction at the axle exerts a constant torque of 0.25 N m that opposes the rotation. What is the magnitude of the disc's angular acceleration?
